conviction_note: The findings sum to +2.3 and lean mildly positive. In their favour: a sourced on-demand price rise of 17-21%, a beat history, a 21%-of-float short and call-side skew. Against them: a sourced but partly priced risk that about 140 MW at Vineland (Microsoft) slips into 2027, which puts the $7-9B year-end ARR target and a Street FY number already $80M above the top of the guide at stake. The scaled number, p_up 55 x abs 13 = +1.3, is smaller than the findings' sum. The print turns on the guide and the first 2027 outlook, whose sign I cannot source. The CoreWeave read-through was already bought (+12% on 2026-11-11).

The two sources agree within 1.2%. EPS consensus is -$0.61. FY2026 company guide: revenue $3.0-3.4B, year-end ARR $7-9B, adj. EBITDA margin about 40%, capex $20-25B, all reaffirmed 2026-08-12 (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/nebius-group-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-12/). FY Street is about $3.48B, roughly $80M above the top of the guide, so the Street already assumes a raise. H1 revenue was $981.3M. Q3 at consensus leaves about $1.5B of Q4 needed to reach the top of the guide.

findings.finding: The Q3 revenue bar of $906-917M (+56-57% QoQ) sits on a name that beat revenue consensus in Q1 2026 ($399.0M vs $388.6M, +2.7%) and Q2 2026 ($582.3M vs $545.1M, +6.8%). Management said on the Q2 call that capacity deployed late in Q2 'begins contributing to revenue in Q3'. A straight ramp from the $3.0B June ARR toward a $7-9B December exit implies an average Q3 run-rate of about $4.0-4.25B, or $1.0-1.06B for the quarter. Consensus at about $910M therefore leaves room for a beat unless the ramp is back-end loaded. Expected print about 3% above the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Rebuilt from confirmed results releases, because the baseline's history is from mismatched 6-Ks. Q2 2026 (2026-08-12, bmo): revenue beat about 7% with the guide reaffirmed, +34.1% (https://finviz.com/news/381592/nebius-shares-surge-34-after-strong-results-raising-questions-over-valuation). Q1 2026 (2026-05-13): revenue beat about 3% with capex raised, +7% to +15.7% depending on source (https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2922038/nebius-stock-up-post-q1-earnings-should-you-buy-hold-or-sell). Q4 2025 (2026-02): pulled back on the print, about -5% from a weak source (https://www.marketbeat.com/articles/nebius-q4-earnings-miss-doesnt-change-its-growth-narrative/). Recent beats have been bought.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus is a public number, and so is the beat history. What is not in the bar is the ramp arithmetic. If the market priced a quarter of $1.0B or more, FY consensus would sit well above $3.48B and previews would talk about a guide raise rather than 'a street above guidance'.
findings.independence: Q2 call guidance on Q3 contribution: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/nebius-group-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-12/. Bar from two estimate sources (TIKR, Earnings Whispers). The Q2 beat size comes from the same release coverage, so it shares a document with this finding.

findings.finding: Delivery risk at Vineland, NJ, the site carrying about $17.4B of Microsoft fees. Aterio satellite imagery dated through 2026-10-21 (reported by Business Insider 2026-11-04) estimates about 140 MW could slip into 2027. The city issued two stop-construction orders on the Bloom fuel cells and LNG tank (2026-08-13). NJ DEP fined DataOne more than $1M for running 62 unpermitted gas generators (2026-09-23). Microsoft said on 2026-10-28 that 'some third-party capacity deliveries we expected in Q1 were delayed' and cut its CY26 capex outlook by about $5B. Bloomberg reported on 2026-11-05 that Microsoft is tightening oversight of Nebius, IREN and Nscale. 140 MW at $20-25M/MW is $2.8-3.5B of ARR, which is large against the $7-9B year-end target. This makes a held-at-low-end or trimmed ARR target, or no FY revenue raise against a Street already $80M above the top, the main downside path.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide has been reaffirmed on every print in 2026 (Feb, May, Aug), never cut, so this name has no history of a guide cut. Q3 2025's print fell as investors questioned the ARR path (https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/2791141/nebius-shares-fall-post-q3-earnings:-should-investors-hold-or-sell). The two news shocks on this line moved the stock -6.3% (Aterio, 2026-11-04) and more than -16% (Bloomberg, 2026-11-05).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock fell about 22% across 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 on this cluster, then recovered most of it on CoreWeave. Nebius has made no statement since, and the print is its first chance to quantify Vineland timing. If the market had priced a trimmed ARR target, the skew would be put-bid rather than -3.55, and the stock would not have taken back +12% on a peer's beat the day before.
findings.independence: Separate sources for each leg. Microsoft capex comment: https://blockspace.media/insight/iren-delays-microsoft-capital-spending/. Bloomberg via https://aiweekly.co/alerts/microsoft-pulls-back-from-neocloud-bets-with-nscale-nebius-iren (2026-11-05). Contract terms with termination and late-delivery damages: https://magica.com/news/microsoft-reviews-neocloud-partners-as-delivery-risks-mount (2026-11-06). DEP fine: https://whyy.org/articles/vineland-data-center-fined/ (2026-09-23). Stop-work orders: https://cryptobriefing.com/nebius-vineland-data-center-second-stop-construction-order/ (2026-08-13). Microsoft did not name Nebius, and Business Insider says the projects 'could be' responsible.

findings.finding: Nebius raised its on-demand GPU list prices effective 2026-10-01: H100 $3.85 to $4.50 (+17%), H200 $4.50 to $5.40 (+20%), B200 $7.15 to $8.50 (+19%), B300 $7.85 to $9.50 (+21%). The new prices are live on nebius.com/prices today. Preemptible capacity moved to a floating spot price capped just under on-demand. This lands on Q4 revenue and on pricing commentary and the 2027 outlook, and points to demand above supply.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the Q2 call management cited short-term deals at $40-50M/MW and an auction clearing 15% above its prior top Blackwell price. The print that carried that commentary rose +34%.
findings.why_not_priced: The rise was observed by a pricing tracker and not issued as a press release, and it is absent from every preview found (Earnings Whispers, TIKR). On-demand is a minority of revenue, against long-term contracts at $20-25M/MW. If the market had priced it, previews would cite rising unit pricing as a Q4 upside lever.
findings.independence: The company page confirms the new prices: https://nebius.com/prices (fetched 2026-11-11). Peer pricing points the same way: IREN contract pricing rose 11-12% (https://www.tikr.com/blog/nebius-soars-7-as-a-rivals-ai-cloud-beat-lifts-neoclouds-after-reactionary-selloff, 2026-11-06).

findings.finding: CoreWeave reported Q3 2026 after the close on 2026-11-10. Revenue was $3.66B against about $3.54B consensus, backlog rose to $132.5B from $104B, and the FY26 revenue guide was raised to $13.0-13.3B. The low end of capex was raised because deployment ran faster than planned. The CEO cited '10x as much qualified demand as available capacity through the end of 2027'. This is the closest peer speaking after Nebius last spoke.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Peer read-throughs move NBIS hard: +12% premarket on 2026-11-11 on this print, and +7% on 2026-11-06 on IREN's beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: NBIS is +11.9% over 5 days and was up about 12% premarket on 2026-11-11. What remains is that CoreWeave cited no third-party delivery slippage, which weakens the 'neocloud execution' bear narrative going into Nebius's own call.
findings.independence: The CoreWeave release: https://investors.coreweave.com/news/news-details/2026/CoreWeave-Reports-Strong-Third-Quarter-2026-Results/default.aspx. This is a peer proxy and not a Nebius number.

findings.finding: IREN on 2026-11-05 moved its $4B+ annualised revenue target from year-end to January. It blamed 'a customer-requested design change and supplier timing', and the customer is identified as Microsoft. In the same report its contract pricing rose 11-12% and a new 5-year deal was signed at about $22M/MW, inside Nebius's $20-25M/MW range. This is a template for how a Microsoft-driven slip shows up: a target pushed by weeks, not cut, while pricing holds.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NBIS fell about 15% on the day of the Microsoft/IREN news and rose +7% the next day after IREN's print.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced through the 2026-11-05/06 swings. What is unpriced is whether Nebius copies IREN's 'slip by a month' framing for its December ARR target. The market's reaction to IREN, a rebound, suggests a short slip with pricing intact is tolerated.
findings.independence: IREN detail: https://finimize.com/content/iren-beat-revenue-estimates-as-microsoft-pushed-back-projects. This is a peer proxy. It shares the Microsoft-delay theme with the Vineland finding but rests on a different company's document.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-22 Nebius signed a $3.5B 364-day senior secured facility with Citi (SOFR +2.75% rising to max 3.50%) for data-centre development and GPU procurement. The 6-K exhibit says it gives 'flexibility over the timing and structure of future external capital raises for growth in 2027 and beyond'. Earlier funding: an ATM that raised about $2.8B at about $224 per share, a $775M ABS facility, more than $9B of expected 2026 prepayments, and $8B of cash at June 30.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prior funding (ATM, converts, NVIDIA's $2B in March) has not been sold on prints. The Q2 print with $2.86B of financing inflows rose +34%.
findings.why_not_priced: The facility is public. What it buys is capacity against more than $40B of investment-grade contracted backlog, so it is a ramp signal and not distress. It also lowers the odds of an ATM at about $158, which is a risk previews name ('possible share sales to raise capital'). The 364-day tenor means refinancing in 2027. If dilution fear were fully gone, the stock would not trade at 5.4-5.9x forward sales against a 10.6x five-year average.
findings.independence: Backlog and prepayments are in the Q2 call coverage: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/nebius-group-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-08-12/. ATM figure: https://www.earningswhispers.com/article/NBIS/22887.

findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price, but a squeeze is only triggered by the print. The latest public settlement (about 10-30) was not found, so this does not net the 5-day rally.

findings.finding: Management promised formal 2027 guidance 'later in the year' (Q2 call, 2026-08-12), so this call is the likely venue for a first guide. Bars: TIKR consensus of $12.24B 2027 revenue (2026-10-21), and BNP Paribas and William Blair at about $22B ARR exiting 2027. Supporting capacity: 5 GW contracted-power target, more than 1 GW a year of new builds from 2027, a 50 MW AIB lease (2026-10-02) with its first hall within 10 months, and the CEO's claim (2026-09-22) that he could 'sell today our entire 2027 capacity'. The sign is unsourced. This is filed for scale: it raises the likely move rather than setting its direction.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior first-year guide on this business model. The Feb 2026 print that set the 2026 targets drew a pullback.
findings.why_not_priced: The 2027 bar is disputed: the $12.24B revenue consensus sits against sell-side exit-ARR calls near $22B. A guide could land on either side of a market that cannot agree on a number. It is not dated with certainty to this call and could come in February.

findings.finding: Insider Form 4 sales in September and October 2026 are small and pre-planned. Example: director John Boynton sold 333 shares at $173.07 on 2026-10-29 under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2026-03-06, and still holds 403,189. Six Form 144s were filed over the period.
findings.why_not_priced: Immaterial: pre-scheduled plan sales, tiny against 25M shares of daily volume.

baseline_tension: The mild positive agrees with the call-side skew (-3.55) and the crowded short. It cuts against the 20-day -14.9% drawdown and the Microsoft/Vineland news that caused it. The +11.9% 5-day run-up means the peer read-through is already in the price.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (crowded short, call-side skew): shrank the Vineland/Microsoft guidance negative from -2.0 to -1.5 and the IREN read-through from -0.5 to -0.3, since 20.8% of float is short and the skew is upside-paid.

Rule 9 (segment net of the rest): Vineland/Microsoft is one customer (about $17.4B of more than $40B backlog, with Meta about $27B ramping separately). This supports the smaller negative and was applied once, not stacked.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the Citi facility funds visible contracted demand, so it is kept as a small positive (+0.3).
Rule 6 (bar): the bar is two agreeing sources ($906M / $916.8M), so no cap was needed. FY Street above the top of the guide is stated in bar.
Last section (wrong-event history): the reaction base rate was rebuilt from confirmed releases (Q2 +34%, Q1 +7-16%, Q4'25 about -5%) instead of the baseline's 6-K matches.
